findings.description: The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. The new `rule_key` returns 1 for any rule that is not of the form `Bash(...)`. In the two jq read loops the call is guarded with `|| continue`, but in the requirements loop it is a bare statement: `rule_key "$perm"`. If `all_required` ever contains a non-Bash requirement (e.g. a `Read(...)`, `WebFetch(...)`, or any malformed entry), `set -e` aborts `main` with no report and a non-zero exit, instead of reporting that rule as missing. The replaced `base_pattern_of` never failed, so this is a new abort path. Even without set -e, `RULE_KEY` would carry the previous iteration's value and silently mis-classify the rule.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight permission check exits abruptly without output when a required rule is not Bash(...)-shaped; callers that gate on the report treat it as a crash rather than a missing-permission result.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the call: `rule_key "$perm" || { missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; }` (or reset RULE_KEY and treat the raw string as an exact key for non-Bash rules), and add a bats case with a non-Bash required rule.

findings.cross_file_justification: .run/platform-features.json is written by .claude/scripts/detect-platform-features.sh (in this diff, truncated) and read by other consumers; the hook now unconditionally rewrites one of its keys.
findings.description: The recorder merges `{active_skill_available: false, active_skill_seen_at, active_skill_source: "tool_input"}` into platform-features.json. `active_skill_available: false` is a hard-coded assertion, not an observation, and it overwrites whatever detect-platform-features.sh had determined. The header comment says the recorder is "evidence only and never changes the mode", yet it does change a field that the previous mode logic (and possibly loa-status.sh / other readers) consumed. The trigger is also model-authored: any Write/Edit payload whose `tool_input` happens to carry `active_skill` permanently stamps the file (one-shot, since `active_skill_seen_at` then exists), so a single spoofed payload fixes the evidence forever until the file is deleted.
findings.failure_mode: A probe-derived `active_skill_available: true` from detect-platform-features.sh is clobbered to false by the first lead-session write carrying active_skill; downstream readers see contradictory evidence (`available: false` alongside `seen_at` set).
findings.suggested_fix: Only add `active_skill_seen_at` and `active_skill_source`; do not touch `active_skill_available` (or set it only when the key is absent via `$b + {...} | .active_skill_available //= false`). Confirm detect-platform-features.sh and loa-status.sh in this diff agree on who owns that key.

findings.description: Defaults change from raw vendor ids (`gpt-4o`, `claude-3-opus-20240229`) to catalog aliases (`reviewer`, `opus`). Aliases only resolve if the request goes through cheval / model-invoke. The old defaults were vendor-shaped and were never updated in the cycle-103 migration that moved flatline-learning-extractor.sh onto model-invoke (that file carries the T1.6/AC-1.4 comment; this one does not), which suggests this script may still hit the OpenAI/Anthropic HTTP APIs directly. If so, the vendor rejects `model: reviewer` / `model: opus` with a 400/404 and the review fails on every run.
findings.failure_mode: Flatline proposal review errors at the provider with an unknown-model response whenever the operator has not set LOA_GPT_MODEL / LOA_OPUS_MODEL.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the dispatch path in flatline-proposal-review.sh. If it calls the vendor APIs directly, either route it through model-invoke (as the extractor does) or resolve the alias via generated-model-maps.sh before the request; add a bats check that the defaults resolve.

findings.description: The fallback allowlist now admits `cheap`, and the widened pattern `^claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)-[0-9]+([-.][0-9]+)?$` admits the dotted form `claude-opus-5.5`. The hard-coded `MODEL_TO_PROVIDER_ID` map in the same file gains `opus`, `fable`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-sonnet-5` but not `cheap` or `claude-opus-5.5`, even though the catalog's backward_compat_aliases does map `claude-opus-5.5`. In the fallback branch (generated maps missing) a model that passes `validate_model` then has no provider id.
findings.failure_mode: With generated-model-maps.sh absent, `flatline_protocol.models.* = cheap` or `claude-opus-5.5` passes validation and then dispatches with an empty provider id, failing later with a less clear error than the allowlist was meant to give.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `["cheap"]="anthropic:claude-sonnet-5"` and `["claude-opus-5.5"]="anthropic:claude-opus-5-5"` to the fallback map, or have validate_model also require a MODEL_TO_PROVIDER_ID hit when the generated maps are not loaded.
